note: Omniscience/omnipresence + zeal + self-offering; interior known, formed, examined

dims.v: the inmost thought-life lies open, discerned from afar before it forms
v2: 'you DISCERN my thoughts from afar' - the interior read at a distance, before the thought consolidates; the mind is transparent, not private.
a word is fully known before it is spoken, the nascent utterance already read
v4: 'before a word is on my tongue you know it ALTOGETHER' - speech is known in its pre-verbal interior form; the inner draft is exposed.
the mind confronts a knowledge it cannot attain and recoils from its own limit
v6: 'such knowledge is too WONDERFUL for me; it is HIGH, I cannot attain it' - the operation is the mind reaching, failing, and knowing its ceiling.
the impulse to escape God's presence tests every direction and finds no exit
v7: 'where shall I FLEE from your presence?' - the interior movement is the tested urge to get away, resolving into the discovery that omnipresence forecloses flight.
the inmost seat of emotion/conscience is woven in the womb, the self prior to itself
v13: 'you formed my INWARD PARTS (kidneys=seat)' - the interior seat is the thing being made; the self is authored before it can author.
recognition of being fearfully made overflows into thanksgiving-praise
v14: 'I PRAISE you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made' - the operation is wonder turned to thanks; the self marvels at its own making.
the soul inwardly acknowledges and settles the truth of God's wonderful works
v14: 'my SOUL knows it very well' - not new information but the interior settling/owning of the truth; the deepest self ratifies it.
God's thoughts are weighed and found precious, vast beyond counting
v17: 'how PRECIOUS to me are your thoughts' - the operation is valuation: the interior appraises and treasures, then is overwhelmed by the sum.
consciousness returns from sleep and finds the God-presence unbroken
v18: 'when I AWAKE, I am still with you' - the operation is the seamless continuity of the God-ward self across the break of sleep.
the bloodthirsty carry a settled murderous disposition the psalmist recoils from
v19: 'O that you would slay the WICKED... men of BLOOD' - the disposition read is the wicked's own murderous bent, the object of the psalmist's recoil.
the self actively commands distance from bloodthirsty men, drawing a line
v19: 'DEPART from me, you bloodthirsty men' - the interior act of severance: the self expels the company of evil, an aversive self-positioning.
the enemies carry a calculated malice, scheming while invoking God's name in vain
v20: 'they speak against you with MALICIOUS INTENT' - the wicked's interior is deliberate scheming, not mere impulse; premeditated hostility.
the psalmist's aversion binds itself to God's cause - hating those who hate God
v21: 'do I not HATE those who hate you?' - the operation is loyalty-aversion: the interior fastens its hatred to God's enemies as an extension of allegiance.
the enemies carry an active hatred DIRECTED at God, the thing the psalmist opposes
v21: 'those who HATE you' - read distinct from the psalmist's hate: this is the enemies' own aversion aimed at God, the disposition the psalmist's loyalty-hate answers.
a visceral loathing rises against those who rise up against God
v21: 'do I not LOATHE those who rise up against you?' - a stronger, gut-level revulsion than hate; the body of the affect intensifies.
the hatred is brought to total, unqualified completeness - no reservation left
v22: 'I HATE them with COMPLETE hatred' - the operation is the totalising of the affect; every reservation is burned off, the aversion is whole.
the aversion has hardened from act into a fixed, owned disposition
v22: 'I count them my ENEMIES' - the noun marks the affect become a standing disposition; hate is now a settled orientation, not a flare.
after the zeal, the self turns the searchlight inward, exposing its own heart
v23: 'SEARCH me, O God, and know my HEART' - the operation reverses: having judged others, the self submits its own interior to examination.
the disquieting/anxious thoughts are laid bare for testing, nothing withheld
v23: 'try me and know my THOUGHTS (disquieting cares)' - the anxious, divided cares are surrendered; the self hides no unease from the test.
the self invites detection of any idolatrous/hurtful way within, wanting it found and led out
v24: 'see if there be any GRIEVOUS (hurtful/idolatrous) way in me' - the operation is a requested interior audit: expose the wrong so it can be replaced by the everlasting way.
v1: God has SEARCHED me - the exhaustive investigation that yields the known interior.
v1: 'and KNOWN me' - the result of the search; total acquaintance with the person.
v2: 'you KNOW when I sit down and rise up' - God's tracking of the whole daily self.
v2: God DISCERNS the thoughts - the act by which the interior is read.
v3: 'you SEARCH OUT my path' - God's winnowing scrutiny of conduct.
v3: 'ACQUAINTED with all my ways' - God's intimate familiarity with the life.
v4: 'you KNOW it altogether' - the completeness of God's knowledge of the word.
v5: 'you HEM me in behind and before' - God's enclosing that provokes the sense of a knowledge too high.
v5: 'you LAY your hand upon me' - the pressing nearness behind the overwhelmed 'too high'.
v10: 'even there your hand shall LEAD me' - the presence that meets the would-be fugitive.
v10: 'your right hand shall HOLD me' - the grasp that forecloses escape.
v13: 'you FORMED my inward parts' - the authoring act on the inmost seat.
v16: 'your eyes SAW my unformed substance' - God's sight of the self before it was formed.
v14/15: God's knowing that the soul acknowledges; the divine knowledge the soul owns.
v19: 'O that you would SLAY the wicked' - the petition addressed to God, not the psalmist's own act.
v23: 'SEARCH me, O God' - the divine act the psalmist now invites onto himself.
v23: 'and KNOW my heart' - the requested divine knowledge of the offered interior.
v23: 'TRY me' - the testing/assaying act invited onto the anxious thoughts.
v23: 'and KNOW my thoughts' - the divine knowing of the surrendered cares.
v24: 'SEE if there be any grievous way' - the divine inspection the self requests.
v24: 'LEAD me in the way everlasting' - God's leading out of the grievous way once found.
